([ABBV](https://app.tikr.com/stock/about?cid=141885706&tid=225079155&ref=q2enxr)) delivered first-quarter 2026 revenues of $15 billion following its April 29 earnings call, beating Wall Street estimates by $300 million and marking a 12% year-over-year acceleration that signals the Humira loss-of-exclusivity transition is structurally complete.

AbbVie raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $14.08 to $14.28, up $0.12 from the prior midpoint.

AbbVie’s revenue reached $15 billion in Q1 2026, growing 12% year-over-year.

Operating income reached $4.82 billion in Q1 2026, growing 19% year-over-year and outpacing revenue growth by seven percentage points.
The GAAP operating margin printed at 32% in Q1 2026, down from the prior quarter’s 34% but above the eight-quarter trough of 29%.

AbbVie has maintained GAAP operating margins above 30% across every year in the peer set, posting 35% in fiscal 2025 against Johnson & Johnson’s ([JNJ](https://app.tikr.com/stock/transcript?cid=141885706&tid=225079155&e=1992650176&ts=3708661&ref=q2enxr)) 28% and Pfizer’s ([PFE](https://app.tikr.com/stock/transcript?cid=141885706&tid=225079155&e=1992650176&ts=3708661&ref=q2enxr))
